note: The harness always enables PROXY parsing, so any input starting with a valid signature reaches the proxy parser.
The harness only finalizes inputs containing an HTTP terminator, so the candidate includes a full request after the PROXY header.
The first bytes are parsed as a PROXY frame before HTTP parsing begins.
The attacker controls the PROXY v2 header fields, including the family and declared length.

code: if (LIKELY(hdr->cmd_ver == PROXY)) { if (hdr->fam == TCP4) ... else if (hdr->fam == TCP6) ... }
note: Selecting TCP6 forces the parser through the larger address-copying branch and exercises the code handling the longest PROXY v2 address payload.
After accepting the frame, the parser advances by the attacker-chosen length, moving the HTTP parser to the crafted tail bytes.
The adjusted scan over the remaining region can step beyond the intended request contents when the declared length and actual bytes disagree.
